18.1.crux: Air pollution happens when air is contaminated by unwanted substances (pollutants) that harm living and non-living things.

cards.title: What clean air contains
say: The small remaining part includes carbon dioxide, argon, methane, ozone and water vapour.

cards.title: Air pollution
say: When unwanted substances change the air in a harmful way, the air is polluted.
The substances that pollute it are called pollutants.
cards.remember: Pollutants = substances that contaminate the air.

cards.title: Where pollutants come from

cols.head: Natural sources
cells: Smoke and dust from forest fires

say: Most air pollution today comes from human activities.

crux_points: Clean air is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen.
Air pollution is contamination of air by harmful substances.
Pollutants come from natural sources and, mostly, human activities.

quiz.q: Which gas makes up most of the air?
A substance that contaminates the air is called a…

18.2.crux: Vehicles, factories and power plants release pollutants like carbon monoxide, sulphur dioxide, nitrogen oxides, soot and CFCs that harm our health and the ozone layer.

cards.title: Main air pollutants

cols.head: Carbon monoxide
cells: Incomplete burning of petrol and diesel

say: Thermal power plants also give out fly ash, a fine dust.

cards.title: Smog
say: In winter, a thick layer of smog hangs over many cities.
It contains nitrogen oxides and causes asthma, coughing and wheezing in children.

cards.title: CFCs and the ozone layer

steps.text: CFCs were used in refrigerators, ACs and aerosol sprays
They rise high into the atmosphere
They damage the ozone layer, which protects us from harmful UV rays

say: Thinning of the ozone layer is often called the 'ozone hole'.
CFCs are now being replaced by less harmful chemicals.

cards.title: Vehicles add up
say: The more vehicles burn fuel, the more pollutants enter the air.

crux_points: Carbon monoxide (vehicles) is poisonous; sulphur dioxide (power plants) harms lungs.
Smog (smoke + fog) causes breathing problems.
CFCs damage the ozone layer that protects us from UV rays.

quiz.q: Which pollutant damages the ozone layer?
quiz.why: Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) destroy ozone high in the atmosphere.

18.3.crux: Acid rain from sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide is eating away the white marble of the Taj Mahal, and soot is turning it yellow.

cards.title: How acid rain forms

steps.text: Industries near Agra give out sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide
These gases mix with water vapour in the air
They form sulphuric acid and nitric acid
The acids fall with rain: acid rain

say: Industries around Agra include rubber processing, car, chemical and the Mathura oil refinery.

cards.title: Marble cancer
say: The Taj Mahal, one of the world's most famous monuments, is being damaged by pollution.

cards.title: Steps to protect it

items.sub: Industries to switch to CNG and LPG
For vehicles in the Taj zone

say: Acid rain also harms crops, soil and other buildings.

crux_points: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide form acids with water vapour: acid rain.
Acid rain corrodes marble ('marble cancer'); soot yellows it.
Cleaner fuels (CNG, LPG) and unleaded petrol help protect the Taj Mahal.

quiz.why: Acids in rain react with and corrode marble.

quiz.q: Which fuels were industries near the Taj asked to switch to?
quiz.why: CNG and LPG are cleaner fuels that pollute much less.

18.4.crux: Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide trap the Sun's heat and keep the Earth warm; too much of them is causing global warming.

cards.title: The greenhouse effect
say: Sunlight warms the Earth, and the Earth gives off heat.
Greenhouse gases trap part of this heat, keeping the Earth warm enough for life.

cards.title: Like a greenhouse

steps.text: In a glass greenhouse, sunlight gets in
The heat can't easily get out
So it stays warm inside, even in winter

say: Carbon dioxide and other gases do this for the whole Earth.

cards.title: Global warming

steps.text: Burning fuels and cutting forests add carbon dioxide
More heat is trapped: the Earth's average temperature rises
Glaciers melt (the Gangotri glacier is shrinking)
Sea level rises and coastal areas may flood

say: Global warming also affects rainfall, farming, forests and wildlife.
cards.remember: Too much greenhouse gas → global warming.

cards.title: Countries working together

items.sub: An agreement by many countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions

say: Global warming is a worldwide problem that needs worldwide action.

crux_points: Greenhouse gases (CO₂, methane, water vapour) trap the Sun's heat.
Some trapping keeps Earth warm; too much causes global warming.
Global warming melts glaciers, raises sea level and disturbs climate.

quiz.q: What is marked '?' in the picture?
quiz.why: Greenhouse gases like CO₂ form the layer that traps heat.

quiz.q: Which of these is a greenhouse gas?
quiz.why: Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere.

18.5.crux: We can reduce air pollution with cleaner fuels, less driving, more public transport, clean energy and more trees.

cards.title: Cleaner energy
say: Switching from fossil fuels to cleaner sources reduces pollutants.

cards.title: What you can do
say: Small actions by many people make a big difference.
Van Mahotsav is a tree-planting festival held every year in July.
cards.remember: Cleaner fuel, fewer vehicles, more trees.

cards.title: Trees clean the air
say: Trees take in carbon dioxide and give out oxygen.

crux_points: Use cleaner fuels (CNG, unleaded petrol) and clean energy (solar, wind, hydro).
Walk, cycle, use public transport and share rides.
Don't burn leaves; plant trees; keep vehicles pollution-checked.

quiz.why: Fewer vehicles on the road means fewer pollutants.

quiz.q: Which is a clean energy source?
quiz.why: Solar energy gives power without burning fuel.

18.6.crux: Water pollution is when harmful substances like sewage, toxic chemicals and silt get into water and make it unsafe for life.

cards.title: Water pollution
say: When harmful substances contaminate water, it is called water pollution.
cards.remember: Water pollution = harmful substances in water.

cards.title: The Ganga

steps.text: The Ganga flows past many towns and cities
Garbage, sewage, dead bodies and industrial waste are put into it
In 1985 the Ganga Action Plan was started to reduce its pollution

say: Rivers are shared by millions of people, plants and animals.

cards.title: Everything in the water suffers

items.sub: From drinking or using dirty water

say: Clean water is precious for every living thing.

crux_points: Water pollution is contamination of water by harmful substances.
Sewage, chemicals and silt are common pollutants.
The Ganga Action Plan (1985) aimed to clean the Ganga.

quiz.q: When did the Ganga Action Plan begin?
quiz.why: It was launched in 1985 to reduce pollution in the river.
Sewage carries germs and harmful substances into water.

18.7.crux: Water gets polluted by factory chemicals, untreated sewage, farm chemicals that cause too much algae, and hot water from power plants.

cards.title: Sources of water pollution

items.name: Industries
items.eg: Harmful chemicals like arsenic, lead, fluorides

items.name: Untreated sewage
items.eg: Germs that cause cholera, typhoid, jaundice

items.name: Farm chemicals
items.eg: Pesticides and fertilisers washed into water

say: Many factories empty their waste into rivers without treating it, though laws forbid this.

cards.title: Too much algae

steps.text: Fertilisers wash from fields into a lake
Extra nutrients make algae grow very fast
When the algae die, decomposers use up the oxygen in the water
Fish and other water life die for lack of oxygen

say: Too many nutrients can be as harmful as too few.
cards.remember: Fertilisers in water → algae boom → oxygen falls → fish die.

cards.title: Hidden pollution

items.sub: Chemicals seep down into the ground

say: Pollution we can't see, in groundwater or in water temperature, is also dangerous.

crux_points: Industries release toxic chemicals; untreated sewage spreads disease.
Fertilisers cause algae to grow fast, then oxygen falls and fish die.
Hot water and chemicals seeping into groundwater also pollute.

quiz.q: Why do fish die after too much algae grows in a lake?
options: Dead algae decompose and use up oxygen
quiz.why: Decomposers breaking down the dead algae use up the water's oxygen.

quiz.q: Which disease can spread through water polluted by sewage?
quiz.why: Sewage carries germs that cause cholera, typhoid and jaundice.

18.8.crux: Potable water is water safe to drink; at home we make it safe by filtering, boiling or adding chlorine.

cards.title: Potable water

cols.head: Potable
cells: Free from germs and harmful substances

cols.head: Not potable
cells: May look clear but carry germs

say: Water that looks clean can still contain germs.

cards.title: Making water safe

items.name: Filtration
items.eg: Removes dirt; candle-type filters are common at home

items.name: Chlorination
items.eg: Chlorine tablets or bleaching powder kill germs

say: Filtration is a physical method; chlorination is a chemical method.

cards.title: Don't overdo chlorine

items.sub: Follow the instructions on the pack
Keep purified water covered and clean

say: Too much chlorine is also not good for health.

crux_points: Potable water is water safe for drinking.
Filtration removes dirt; boiling and chlorination kill germs.
Use chlorine in the right amount.

quiz.q: Water that is safe to drink is called…
Which method KILLS germs in water?
options: Pouring it into a new jug
quiz.why: Boiling kills germs; chlorination does too.

18.9.crux: We can keep water clean by treating waste before it reaches rivers and by reducing, reusing and recycling water at home.

cards.title: What industries must do

steps.text: Factory waste water is collected
It is treated to remove harmful chemicals
Only then may it go into rivers or lakes

say: Laws require industries to treat their waste, but they must be followed strictly.

cards.title: Reduce, reuse, recycle water

items.sub: Water used to wash vegetables can water plants
Fats and oils block drains and pollute
Treated waste water can be used again

say: Every drop saved is less water to clean.

cards.title: Spread the word
say: Clean water depends on everyone's habits.

crux_points: Industrial waste must be treated before it is released.
At home: save, reuse and recycle water; don't pour oil down drains.
Awareness helps everyone protect water.

quiz.q: Water used to wash vegetables can be reused to…
quiz.why: It's fine for plants, so reusing it saves water.

quiz.q: Why shouldn't cooking oil be poured down the sink?
options: It blocks drains and pollutes water
quiz.why: Oils and fats clog pipes and pollute water bodies.
